note: Validation corpus for the bpm-test-ownership@1 capability. Truth here is HUMAN/MANUAL and is used to validate the specialist; it is never a production detector. Aliases are synthetic. This file lives under tools/ because it carries the real rule's semantics, and tools/ is one of the two locations the employer-specifics gate excludes.

rule.semantics: The owner attribute is required on test CLASSES and on test METHODS. Combined attribute lists and DataTestMethod/DataRow forms are in scope.
rule.notes: The rule governs declarations only. Invocations, comments and assignments are out of its reach and must be accounted for as notInReach, never as compliant.

expectationVocabulary.violation: The declaration is in the rule's reach and lacks the owner attribute.
expectationVocabulary.compliant: The declaration is in the rule's reach and carries the owner attribute.
expectationVocabulary.notInReach: The construct is not a test declaration the rule governs.
expectationVocabulary.notRouted: The file does not select the ownership pack at all, so no verdict is produced for it.
expectationVocabulary.unknown: Required declaration context could not be established. Never a finding, never compliant.

cases.description: Nine new [TestMethod] declarations added with no owner attribute. This is the live change set the capability must reproduce.
Owner attribute present in its own bracket group.
Owner attribute inside a combined bracket group. Before the lexer fix this read as TestMethod alone, so a compliant declaration was reported as a violation - an invented finding, not a missed one.
The rule covers classes as well as methods; both carry the attribute here.
A test class with no owner attribute. Confirms class scope, which the target repository's weaker methods-only phrasing would have missed.
DataTestMethod with a DataRow whose argument list contains a comma. The comma is an argument separator, not an attribute separator.
